definitions.explanation: The hard outer covering of a shellfish or mollusk. Often found on beaches and collected as souvenirs or decorations.

examples.japanese: {貝殻|かいがら}を{集|あつ}める。
{海岸|かいがん}できれいな{貝殻|かいがら}を{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: I found a beautiful seashell on the beach.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちが{貝殻|かいがら}を{拾|ひろ}って{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: The children are playing picking up seashells.

notes:
{貝殻|かいがら} is the hard outer covering left behind by mollusks and other shellfish. Seashells washed up on beaches are a common sight in Japan, and {貝殻|かいがら}{拾|ひろ}い (shell collecting) is a popular seaside activity for children and adults alike.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {貝|かい} (shellfish) + {殻|がら} (shell, husk)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {貝殻|かいがら}を{拾|ひろ}う (to pick up seashells)
- {貝殻|かいがら}を{集|あつ}める (to collect seashells)
- {貝殻|かいがら}の{形|かたち} (the shape of a shell)
- {貝殻|かいがら}で{飾|かざ}る (to decorate with seashells)

RELATED WORDS:
- {貝|かい} (shellfish — the living animal)
- {殻|から} (shell, husk — general term; read から when standalone)
- {巻|ま}き{貝|がい} (snail shell, spiral shell)
- {二枚貝|にまいがい} (bivalve)
